title: Arsenal's £66m Nusa question and the Chelsea noise
body:
Arsenal could be asked to pay £66m for RB Leipzig's Antonio Nusa, a figure that turns a transfer target into a test of nerve [S1].

Big fees for players who haven't pulled on your shirt yet deserve a hard stare. The price tag is the first thing to interrogate, not the last.

Chelsea feature in the same gossip round-up, with Real Betis reported to have rejected their bid for Jose Morante [S1]. Elsewhere, Arsenal have been linked with contacting Bournemouth about Alex Scott [S2], while Aston Villa are weighing up a move for Chelsea's Romeo Lavia [S2]. That is a lot of names and very little certainty.

The form tells a clearer story. Arsenal's last five league results read WWWWW: five wins, 15 points, seven goals scored and one conceded [ST1]. Chelsea's run reads WWLWL: three wins, two defeats, nine points, nine scored and four conceded [ST2]. A side on a perfect run has little reason to splash cash on a rumour, and a side with a looser record has more reason to keep shopping. Neither fact forces a deal to happen this week.

The smart money is on patience, because rushed deals rarely age well. The better move is to let the noise pass and see who is still standing when the deadline arrives.

The Touchline Take: judge the business when the window shuts, not before.
